sections.html:
Chesapeake is a Hampton Roads city in southeastern Virginia with no county above it. It had 249,422 residents in 2020, second in the state for population and also second for land area. It is split into six boroughs: South Norfolk, Butts Road, Deep Creek, Pleasant Grove, Western Branch and Washington. Houses range from dense older streets to large rural lots.

The average elevation is only 16 feet, and water runs through the whole city, including the Great Dismal Swamp, the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway and the branches of the Elizabeth River. Ask the city for the flood zone of your parcel before you list, particularly if the lot is near water. Buyers will ask. Crawl space moisture and attic ventilation are also typical inspection items in this humid climate.

The city collects real estate tax every quarter, not twice a year. A deadline on a weekend or holiday slides to the next business day.

If a payment is not postmarked or received by the deadline, penalty and interest are applied as state and city code require. Virginia's ceilings in Code of Virginia 58.1-3916 are 10 percent for the property tax penalty and 10 percent a year for interest, so ask the Treasurer what the city actually charges.

The real estate tax rate for fiscal year 2026 to 2027 is $1.01 per $100 of assessed value, which includes $0.01 for mosquito control. The stormwater fee for a single residence is $136.20 a year, paid in two installments of $68.10.

Under City Code Section 26-372, the owner of the billed parcel pays the stormwater fee. A bill that is unpaid when you list may still be open when you close, so check it with the quarterly tax.

The Treasurer can be emailed at paytax@cityofchesapeake.net, and the city main line is 757-382-2489. The address is 306 Cedar Road, Chesapeake, VA 23322.

sections.h2: How the Assessor sets and changes values
sections.html:
Chesapeake values property as of January 1, and new values take effect July 1. Owners whose value changed are mailed a notice, and for the current cycle those notices go out on or before March 1, 2027.

New construction, additions and demolitions are picked up through supplemental bills, with valuation changes captured on October 1, January 1, April 1 and July 1. A teardown or an addition done before listing can therefore change the bill during the year.

The Assessor's office is at 306 Cedar Road, 4th Floor, phone 757-382-6235, email assessor@cityofchesapeake.net. A free property search is available at chesapeake.civ.quest.

Owners can take three routes, alone or together: a property review with the Assessor, an application to the Board of Equalization, or a petition to the Circuit Court.

  • A Board application must show that the property is valued above fair market value, that the assessment is not applied uniformly, or that it does not follow accepted appraisal standards or Virginia law.
  • The city posts an Appeal Process guide, filing instructions and an application as PDFs.
  • Time limits apply, so ask the Assessor's office for the deadline before you plan.

Start with the property review. A call to 757-382-6235 can catch a data error, such as the wrong square footage, without a formal filing.

sections.h2: Tax relief for seniors and disabled owners
sections.html:
For owners over 65 or disabled, the city runs tax relief through the Commissioner of the Revenue at 757-382-6455, option 4. Applications run from January 1 through May 15. The city listed relief of 100 percent for household income up to $25,000 in fiscal year 2025. Limits are listed by year, so check the current figures before you apply.

A relief approval changes what the next owner would pay, so mention it to your closing agent if it applies to your house.

Four items need a check before closing: this quarter's real estate tax, the stormwater fee, land use enrollment and recordation costs. Virginia does not allow a title transfer when delinquent taxes are paid through a tax lien sale, so back taxes can complicate a sale if they are left too long.

If the land is in the use value program, the minimums are 5 acres for agricultural, horticultural and open space land and 20 acres for forest land. A change in use or a rezoning at the owner's request can trigger rollback taxes covering the current year and the five most recent complete tax years, plus simple interest.

Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents per $500 of value under 58.1-802. Cash Home Buyers can buy a Chesapeake house as is, including one with overdue tax, and the Treasurer's payoff can come out of the proceeds.

sections.h2: Why four payments change a sale
sections.html:
With quarterly billing, the day you close almost never lines up with a due date. Say you close in the weeks after the December 31 payment: the second quarter is paid, the third is coming on March 31, and the buyer and seller have to decide who covers the days in between. The sale contract sets that split, and the closing agent usually figures it from the Treasurer's records.

Stormwater is billed on a different schedule, with halves due June 5 and December 31. Treat it as its own line on the settlement statement and ask whether the half you are in has been paid. The owner of the billed parcel is responsible, so an unpaid half left at closing can end up as a dispute between buyer and seller.

Owners who prefer a simple exit can ask for an as-is cash offer. It does not change the tax math, but it removes the repair list and the showing schedule.

When a bill is overdue, the penalty and interest keep adding up, so the sooner you get a payoff the better. Work in this order: get the payoff in writing from the Treasurer, check the stormwater fee, confirm the land use status, and hand all three to the closing agent. Do not wait for a tax lien sale. Virginia will not allow a title transfer when delinquent taxes are paid that way, which can stall a sale you could have closed cleanly.

Call the Treasurer and ask for the amount due this quarter and the stormwater fee, with a payoff dated to your closing. Then look up your parcel at chesapeake.civ.quest and check the record for errors. If the house has had an addition or a teardown, ask the Assessor when the change will show up on a supplemental bill so the closing agent can prorate correctly.

faqs.q: What are the Chesapeake tax due dates?
faqs.a: In four quarterly payments: September 30, December 31, March 31 and June 5. A date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.
$1.01 per $100 of assessed value for fiscal year 2026 to 2027, including $0.01 for mosquito control.

faqs.q: How can I challenge a Chesapeake assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at 757-382-6235 for a review, apply to the Board of Equalization, or petition Circuit Court. The routes can be combined.

faqs.q: What is the Chesapeake stormwater fee?
faqs.a: For a single residence the city lists $136.20 a year, due in two installments of $68.10 on June 5 and December 31. The owner of the billed parcel pays it.

faqs.q: Is a sale possible with unpaid Chesapeake taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing normally settles the balance from your proceeds, so request a payoff dated to your closing.
